extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, regulated parties, and practitioners seeking NYC DOT rules, notices, or opportunities to comment
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of where NYC DOT's laws, rules, and rulemaking notices are published (Charter, Administrative Code, Rules of the City), plus lists of Notices of Public Hearing and Notices of Adoption and the DOT CAPA regulatory agenda. Useful for locating applicable rules and finding opportunities to comment or review adopted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where NYC laws and rules are published
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws and rules of the City of New York are published in the New York City Charter, the New York City Administrative Code and the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most updated versions of these publications are available on the American Legal Publishing (ALP) website. Visitors may use the "Search" button at the top of the ALP website to find topics across all three publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYC DOT Rulemaking Process (CAPA flowchart)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NYC DOT Rulemaking Process flowchart presents the process by which NYC DOT promulgates a rule pursuant to the City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To learn more about NYC’s rulemaking process or to comment on proposed rules, visit the NYC Rules website.

rubrics_metrics.name: New York City Charter — source of DOT authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York City Charter defines the organization, functions, and essential procedures and policies of NYC government. NYC DOT's authority can be found in Chapter 71 of the New York City Charter.

rubrics_metrics.name: New York City Administrative Code — codified local laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York City Administrative Code contains the codified local laws of New York City enacted by the New York City Council and Mayor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The majority of local laws pertaining to NYC DOT can be found in Title 19 of the New York City Administrative Code; other titles—including, but not limited to—Title 7 and Title 10 contain local laws relevant to NYC DOT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of the City of New York (Title 34) — DOT rules location
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules of the City of New York contain the rules and regulations for New York City Agencies. NYC DOT's rules can be found in Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staten Island Ferry Rules (Chapter 1 of Title 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staten Island Ferry rules can be found in Chapter 1 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Ferry Terminals and Vessels rules on ALP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highway Rules (Chapter 2 of Title 34) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Highway Rules can be found in Chapter 2 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 2 includes rules regarding street construction permits, permit fees, requirements for sidewalk, curb and roadway work, flood mitigation systems, and other related information. Review Highway Rules on ALP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty Schedule (Chapter 3 of Title 34) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: NYC DOT's Penalty Schedule can be found in Chapter 3 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3 lists penalties associated with NYC DOT violations that are adjudicated at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) through the Environmental Control Board (ECB). Review NYC DOT’s Penalty Schedule on ALP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic Rules (Chapter 4 of Title 34) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic Rules can be found in Chapter 4 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4 includes rules regarding traffic signals, parking, bicycles, moped share and carshare, pedestrian plazas, buses, taxi/for-hire vehicles, trucks, and other related information. Review Traffic Rules and Regulations on ALP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocable Consents Rules (Chapter 7 of Title 34) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about Revocable Consents can be found in Chapter 7 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 includes rules about applications, requirements, and fees related to obtaining a revocable consent. Review all Revocable Consents on ALP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Public Hearing and Opportunity to Comment — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Public Hearing list the publication date in the City Record and the date/time of the public hearing, and include a description of the proposed rule (often specifying which sections of Title 34 would be amended). Example phrasing: "The Notice of Public Hearing was published in the City Record on [date]. A public hearing will be held on [date] at [time]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices may indicate whether hearings will be held virtually or in-person; they summarize the proposed change (e.g., which sections would be amended) and provide the opportunity to comment. Examples on the page include proposals relating to busways, speed limits for e-bikes/e-scooters, revocable consents, microhubs, jaywalking, mopeds on bridges, license plate display, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of Adoption describe the adopted rule, cite the sections of the Rules amended, state the date the Notice was published in the City Record, and state the effective date of the adopted rule. Example phrasing: "This adopted rule amends section X of Chapter Y of Title 34... The Notice was published in the City Record on [date]. The rule will go into effect on [date]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include adopted rules for Busways, Adopt-A-Highway Program updates, Open Streets Program, Dining Out NYC, Jaywalking, Mopeds on Bridges, Microhubs, revocable consents for battery swapping cabinets, trade-in programs for mobility devices, and others. Notices typically provide a short summary and the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda (CAPA) — publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Sections 1042 and 1043 of the New York City Charter, NYC DOT publishes a CAPA Regulatory Agenda (e.g., for Fiscal Year 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NYC DOT's regulatory agenda is published in the City Record (example: published on May 1, 2026). For previous regulatory agendas, the page directs readers to visit the City Record and search for "DOT CAPA Regulatory Agenda."
